sources: Composite DTM is approximately 99% England coverage at 1m spatial resolution.
DTM removes surface objects to represent terrain surface.
2022 composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Repeat-survey composite selection uses newest, best-resolution data.
Resampled source data used bilinear interpolation before merge.
2022 DTM composite survey period is 2000-06-06 through 2022-04-02.
Metadata survey index is the official location-to-source-survey lineage record.
Composite vertical accuracy statement is +/-15cm RMSE for constituent surveys.
Dataset exposes survey download, metadata WMS/WFS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API service links.
Dataset creation date is 2023-02-08 and revision date is 2023-12-15.
Composite DSM is approximately 99% England coverage at 1m spatial resolution.
DSM includes surface objects such as buildings, vegetation and vehicles as well as terrain.
DSM composite uses the same Time Stamped plus National Programme lineage model.
DSM repeat-survey selection also states newest, best-resolution source preference.
DSM resampling before merge is documented as bilinear interpolation.
DSM metadata index identifies which survey contributed at a location.
National Data Library record states 5km GeoTIFF tiles aligned to OS National Grid.
DTM values are metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn using OSTN15 transformation.
Data.gov.uk exposes OGC API, WMTS, survey-download and technical-guide links.
DSM National Data Library record states 5km GeoTIFF tiles aligned to OS National Grid.
DSM values are metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn using OSTN15.
DSM record states no public access constraints and Open Government Licence metadata.
Time Stamped DTM archive contains site-specific surveys across England since 1998.
Time Stamped DTM is available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m depending on project requirements.
Time Stamped DTM is distributed as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files.
Time Stamped DTM is in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and aligned to OS Grid.
Time Stamped DTM transformation is survey-time specific rather than universally identical.
Time Stamped DSM archive contains repeated site-specific surveys and multiple resolutions.
Time Stamped DSM metadata index records survey dates and product resolution for a location.
Time Stamped DSM metadata index records transformation and geoidal model used.
Time Stamped DSM vertical accuracy statement is +/-15cm RMSE.
Environment Agency site-specific LIDAR survey history extends back to 1998.
Point-cloud archive availability is described as going back to 2006.
Historical archiving means a surface model need not have a matching point cloud.
Point cloud is distributed in 5km download zip files by survey year.
Coverage metadata provides survey start/end dates and average point-density information.
National LIDAR Programme divided England into 302 Phase-1 survey blocks.
Phase-1 national blocks were captured between January 2017 and February 2023.
Repeat captures receive incrementing phase numbers rather than overwriting survey identity.
Repeat capture is needs-driven rather than a guaranteed complete rolling recapture of every block.
National Programme data is published through the Defra survey portal on an ongoing quarterly basis.
Products are provided in 5km tiles aligned to the Ordnance Survey grid.
Tile naming embeds unique survey id, OS grid reference and first/last survey dates.
Surface models use GeoTIFF while point clouds use LAZ.
Index catalogue provides survey-specific information for each tile.
EA states index catalogues can be downloaded for all survey products.
Index catalogues include information on the time of year data was collected.
LiDAR Composite survey-download zips now use a spatial metadata index in GeoPackage format.
GeoPackage spatial metadata index describes spatial location of raster elevation data.
GeoPackage spatial metadata index describes temporal extent of raster elevation data.
Relevant metadata records provide technical guides for index format and attribute schema.
EA survey data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid.
Elevations are recorded above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
LiDAR Composite is transformed using OSTN15 geoid model according to EA FAQ wording.
Time Stamped and point-cloud metadata catalogues should be consulted for survey-specific geoid model.
EA states surveys after 2016-08-26 use OSGM15 geoid model.
Ground Truth points have stated +/-3cm RMSE accuracy.
Ground Truth attributes include survey date, surface type, survey method, transformation and geoidal models.
Ground Truth may be reused when less than five years old, or three years for coastal projects.
Timestamped survey QC compares RMSE, standard deviation and random error against Ground Truth.
Ground Truth dataset states LIDAR surveys must be under +/-15cm RMSE and 10cm standard deviation/random error to pass QC.
EA FAQ states absolute height error specification is less than +/-15cm RMSE.
EA FAQ separately states expected relative/random height error no more than +/-5cm.
EA FAQ directs users to survey-specific Ground Truth result for a particular survey.
DSP replaced legacy Esri Image Services with open-standard WCS/WMS services.
Service update distinguishes WMS as summarized display and WCS as elevation-providing service.
Composite DSM/DTM feeds were republished with updated endpoints to support future updates.
Composite source selection cannot identify a target survey without consulting metadata index at target location.
Survey-specific resolution, dates and transformation are explicit lineage dimensions for Time Stamped tiles.
Survey-level measured QC must remain distinct from generic composite-wide accuracy statements.
